ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is the input power supply Ui = 20 V, with the upper end positive and the lower end negative; the positive input end passes through a series resistor labeled 1 kΩ and is connected to the upper node. From this node downward there is a parallel branch, with the Zener diode Dz connected to the bottom common negative end; the same node is also connected on the right side to the load resistor RL, labeled 1 kΩ, and the output voltage Uo is marked across RL, upper positive and lower negative. Reasoning: Dz and RL are in parallel, so if Dz enters the reverse breakdown voltage-regulating state, it will clamp the output node voltage at the regulated value Uz. First assume there is no Zener diode action; then by voltage division of the 1 kΩ series resistor and the 1 kΩ load, Uo = 20 V × 1 kΩ / (1 kΩ + 1 kΩ) = 10 V. This voltage is greater than the given regulated voltage 5 V, so the Zener diode will break down, conduct, and clamp the output. Current check: when clamped to 5 V, the series resistor current is (20 - 5)/1 kΩ = 15 mA, the load current is 5/1 kΩ = 5 mA, and the remaining about 10 mA flows through the Zener diode, so the state holds. Therefore Uo = 5 V.
